Land at PEK.basis: PEK airport guides say international arrivals take ~1h to clear fingerprinting/passport control and collect bags (immigration alone 30-60 min), plus deplaning a widebody and the long T2 walk.

Drop bags at Regent Beijing.basis: TripAdvisor reviews of the Regent describe fast, smooth bell-desk luggage storage before check-in; no evidence of queues, so 20 min is a reasoned allowance for tagging and freshening up.

Breakfast.basis: Hotel buffet breakfast; 35 min is enough to eat properly while still making a 07:00 gate slot if you start around 06:30.

Temple of Heaven.basis: TripAdvisor reviews and China travel guides converge on 1-2h for the main halls and 2-3h if you also enjoy the park and the locals exercising; 2h fits the North Gate joint-ticket route.

Lunch.basis: Wulingyuan restaurants are ordered-at-table Hunan places at RMB80-120pp with no English menus; a proper unhurried meal is ~1 h.

Beijing city model.basis: TravelChinaGuide and tour-beijing put the visit at 1-2h, recommending ~40 min on the 1:750 scale model alone before the historical and multimedia floors.

Dinner.basis: Hunan dinner in Wulingyuan is a shared-dish sit-down affair; 1.5 h lets you order, wait and actually enjoy it rather than refuel.

Qianmen & hutongs.basis: Beijing walking guides time the Liulichang-Dashilan-Qianmen stroll at about 1.5h, with 1-2h quoted for a quick wander and half a day only if you shop and eat.

Shichahai lakes.basis: AllTrails logs the Shichahai loop at 2.2 miles / 44 min average walking, and Beijing guides suggest 1-2h to actually soak up the bar lights and lakeside atmosphere at dusk.

Tiananmen Square.basis: Guides say allocate ~2h including queuing, but note non-holiday weekday security waits are under 30 min and before 09:00 is the quietest slot - so ~30 min entry plus 45 min on the square.

Forbidden City.basis: Guides put the central axis at 2-3h and 4-5h if you add the Treasure and Clock galleries; Meridian Gate security is a further 15-20 min off-peak, so 3.5h is the unhurried first-timer figure.

Jingshan Park.basis: Trip.com and TripAdvisor reports give a 5-15 min climb each way (about 150 steps) and an average visit around 30 min, stretching to 2h only for dedicated photographers.

National Museum.basis: TripAdvisor reviewers and museum guides say most people spend 2-3h and enthusiasts 4-6h, with the Ancient China galleries alone quoted at 2-3h; add the passport/security check on entry.

Wangfujing.basis: Guides say half a day to a full day if you seriously shop the malls, but TripAdvisor reviews of the street itself describe an hour-ish wander among stalls, screens and bookstores.

Mutianyu Great Wall.basis: TripAdvisor Q&A and China guides say most visitors spend 2-3h at Mutianyu including the cable car and several watchtowers (3-4h for a thorough hike); the toboggan is counted separately here.

Toboggan down.basis: Rider reports and operator guides put the descent itself at 5-10 min depending on braking; the rest is the walk to the launch platform, the safety briefing and the summer queue.

Sanlitun Taikoo Li.basis: Beijing guides suggest 3-5h to explore both Taikoo Li zones leisurely and 1-2h for a quick pass; with dinner folded in, 2.5h is a realistic evening.

CCTV 'Big Pants'.basis: Guides note interior access is staff-only and visitors typically spend 20-60 min photographing from the open plaza or the free China World Mall viewing terrace. Set to the TOP of that documented range (was 30): this is the stop whose entire value is the tower after dark, it is now scheduled post-sunset, and an hour lets you shoot the plaza and ride up to the mall terrace rather than just stop for one photo.

Mutianyu night tour.basis: The official Mutianyu night session runs 17:30-21:00 with lighting from 19:00 and last ticket check 20:30; operator listings describe roughly a 3.5h on-site sunset-and-lights visit.

Summer Palace.basis: Multiple guides state 3-4h is the minimum for a visit that feels worthwhile and that 2h is only a skim of this very spread-out site; the North Palace Gate to Longevity Hill to ferry route fits 3.5h.

798 Art District.basis: TripAdvisor and district guides give 2h for a highlights loop and 2-4h for a typical visit (4-5h for art devotees); 2.5h covers the outdoor art and smaller galleries with UCCA timed separately.

UCCA.basis: Visitor write-ups say the UCCA halls are compact enough to walk through in about an hour; the extra 15 min covers ticketing and the UCCA Store.

Fly from PKX.basis: Standard guidance is 2h before a domestic departure; PKX guides warn check-in closes 45 min out, security queues run 10-30 min and the 06:00-09:00 window is the airport's busiest.

Hotpot alt · Shu Daxia.basis: TripAdvisor reviewers report 40 min to 2 h waits at Shu Daxia peak dinner (18:00–21:00) on top of a ~1.5–2 h table sitting.

Land at CTU.basis: Chengdu Shuangliu arrival guides say domestic arrivals skip immigration and advise meeters to turn up ~30 min after touchdown.

Check in at Minyoun Dongda.basis: Standard China 4–5 star check-in with passport registration plus getting bags to the room; 24/7 front desk so no wait for staff.

Taikoo Li.basis: Chengdu guides put a relaxed walk through Taikoo Li at 1–2 hours, longer only if you stop to dine.

Daci Temple.basis: Trip.com itinerary allows about an hour for the halls; the compound is small and free, so 45 min covers halls plus the relic room without tea.

IFS rooftop panda.basis: Trip reports note a line forms for close-up photos with the climbing panda even at mall opening, but the terrace itself is one small garden.

Chengdu Panda Base.basis: Guides advise at least 3–4 h because the base is large; walking the whole park is about 3 h, and 2.5 h is described on TripAdvisor as the rushed minimum.

Chengdu Museum.basis: Reviewers report 2 h for a leisurely pass and 3–4 h for the full building; 2.5 h covers the history floors plus the shadow-puppet gallery.

People’s Park.basis: Guides bundle park plus teahouse into 1–2 h; with Heming timed separately, the lake loop and marriage-market corner take about 45 min.

Heming Teahouse.basis: Teahouse sources put the average Heming visit at 1–2 h with no table time limit, and caier ear cleaning adds roughly 20–30 min.

Kuanzhai Alleys.basis: TripAdvisor and Chinese guides recommend 2–3 h for the wide, narrow and well lanes, best from about 17:00 once the lights come on.

Sichuan opera.basis: Shufeng Yayun runs nightly from 20:00 for 80–90 min, with a 19:30 arrival for seating, tea and backstage face-painting.

Chengdu East → Guanghan.basis: Rail guides advise 30–40 min inside Chengdu East for security and ID checks before the ~18 min high-speed hop to Guanghan North.

Hotpot alt · Lao Matou.basis: TripAdvisor reviewer of Lao Matou Yulin waited 90 min then ate for an hour; a mid-evening arrival at this less touristy branch lands nearer 30–45 min queue plus ~1.5 h at table.

Guanghan North.basis: Small suburban station — walk out and join the taxi/shuttle rank; the 15–20 min ride to the museum is travel, not stop time.

Sanxingdui Museum.n: New hall plus old bronze hall
Sanxingdui Museum.basis: Official and tour guidance since the 2023 new building recommends 3–4 h (some say 3–5 h) for the new halls plus the old bronze hall; it is genuinely a half-day.

SKP Chengdu.basis: Visitors describe SKP as a photo/architecture stop rather than a shopping trip — five sunken floors and the rooftop garden take about an hour to walk.

Wuhou Shrine.basis: Chengdu guides state the main sights take about two hours, three if you linger in the gardens or the Three Kingdoms history.

Jinli Old Street.basis: Guides suggest 2–3 h for Jinli at sunset; 1.5 h fits a walk plus snacks when Wuhou Shrine next door is visited the same evening.

Head to Chengdu East.basis: Guidance for Chengdu East, the region's busiest station, is to arrive 30–60 min before departure for security, ID gates and finding the platform; the 45–60 min transfer is travel, not stop time.

Check in at KS Kongshang.basis: Standard China hotel passport registration plus high-rise lift waits in the Xinhua International tower; no venue-specific reports found.

Jiefangbei.basis: Trip.com lists 1-3h and Tripadvisor reviewers say 2-3h for shopping, but a monument-plus-alleys walk without shopping lands at the 1h low end.

Raffles Crystal deck.basis: Trip.com suggests 1-3h and Becksplore's review advises about two hours for deck plus skywalk; 90min covers ticketing, the 47-floor lift and the National Geographic exhibits without the add-on rides.

Chaotianmen Docks.basis: Trip.com recommends 1-2h for the huge ship-shaped square, but a pier stroll plus checking tomorrow's cruise wharf sits at the low end.

Kuixinglou Plaza.basis: Meet Chongqing describes a small free square experienced by crossing one elevated walkway, roughly 30min to an hour with no ticket or lift queue.

Qiansimen Bridge.basis: Free lower pedestrian deck 5min from Hongya Cave's top terrace; a walk-out-and-back photo stop, no queue or ticket.

Jiangbei riverbank.basis: Jiangbeizui Riverside Park viewing platforms face Hongya Cave about 1.25km away; a walk to the platform and photos, not a park circuit.

Hongya Cave.basis: Guides put a full walk-through at 2-3h across 11 levels with the 19:30-22:00 window the most crowded and lift queues of 30-45min (stairs advised); trimmed because the bridge and riverbank photo stops are separate.

Liziba monorail.basis: Chongqing city guides give a suggested stay of 30min at the purpose-built viewing platform, with trains passing every 2-4 minutes so waits are short.

Eling Park.basis: Trip.com suggests 1-2h; the park is small but the Liangjiang Pavilion is a seven-to-nine storey climb worth lingering at for the panorama.

Testbed 2.basis: Trip.com's suggested sightseeing time is 1-3h for the shops, galleries and rooftop of the old printing works; 90min covers a proper wander without a meal.

Baixiang Ju.basis: Guides report most visitors spend 40min to 1.5h, with the main corridors and the three street-level exits coverable in about 20min.

Yangtze Cableway.basis: Ride is only 3.6-5min but queues run 40-60min at peak windows (1-2h on holidays); late August is peak season even with WeChat queue numbers.

Longmenhao Old Street.basis: Trip.com suggests 1-3h for the six-tier hillside precinct and reviewers warn of a lot of stairs; 75min covers the main lanes and viewpoints.

Two Rivers night cruise.basis: Operators state a fixed 45-50min sailing over the 16-20km loop, and Chinese booking guides advise arriving 30min before departure for ticket check and seating.

Chongqing West (alt station).basis: Station guides advise arriving 60-90min before a high-speed departure here, with 15+ minutes of walking from drop-off to gate across the five-level hub.

Chongqing North station.basis: Guides range from a 40min bare minimum to 1.5-2h, with the split North/South squares (one metro stop apart) the main risk factor; 60min is the practical buffer.

Fenghuang HSR station.basis: Fenghuanggucheng is a small line station ~10 km from town; arrival is deboarding, exiting and walking to the bus/taxi forecourt, not a visit.

Check in at Jinshuian.basis: Standard Chinese hotel check-in with passport registration plus bag drop runs 15-25 min; no reviewer reports of long waits at this riverside property.

Fenghuang Ancient Town.basis: Blogs put the core walking loop at '2-3 hours, flexible' including the bridges and stones listed separately here, so the general stroll itself is ~1-1.5h.

East Gate Tower.basis: Only 11 m high with a short preserved wall section and a CNY 5 ticket; foreigner guides estimate 15-20 min and note the exterior is free.

Hong Bridge.basis: Two-storey bridge: shops downstairs, small calligraphy/painting gallery and river viewpoint upstairs; guides estimate 10-15 min, a bit more with the upper floor.

Jumping stones.basis: The tiaoyan is ~100 m of 15 piers and guides say roughly 5 min to cross; early morning avoids the photo queues that slow it at midday.

Bar street.basis: Reviewers describe KTV-style bars, very loud music and mostly empty rooms, so it is a walk-through plus one drink rather than a long night out.

Station shuttle / taxi.basis: Station is ~10 km out: the CNY 7 express bus takes about 20 min and a taxi 17-20 min, plus a few minutes to find/queue for it.

Tuojiang night boat.basis: Operators and guides consistently give the round trip as ~20-25 min (North Gate wharf to Wanming Pagoda and back); allow the rest for boarding.

Wanming Pagoda.basis: A seven-storey Qing brick tower viewed from the riverside lanes, not entered; trip reports treat it purely as a night photo stop.

Snow Bridge (Xueqiao).basis: Two-tier Huang Yongyu pavilion bridge whose upper level is the viewpoint; blogs describe climbing it to watch the town light up, a short stop.

Sunrise / mist session.basis: Photo guides put the empty, misty window at roughly 06:00-07:00 before the town wakes, which is about a 45-min shooting session.

Nanhua Bridge.basis: Guides list it as the premium elevated vantage you climb for the panorama; it is a viewpoint stop with nothing to tour.

Shen Congwen Residence.basis: A ~600 sqm two-court siheyuan of 11 small rooms; Chinese reviews say there is little beyond furniture, manuscripts and photos, so visits are short.

Miao batik & silver lanes.basis: Shopping guides allow 1-2h for serious buying, but warn much street 'silver' is nickel alloy; a browsing pass of the lanes is ~30 min.

Ginger candy stalls.basis: Guides describe free tasting and the hand-pulling demo as a 10-15 min stop, with bags at CNY 15-30.

Head to the station.basis: Chinese high-speed stations want you inside ~30 min ahead and foreigners often need the manual passport lane; gates close 5 min before departure, so 45 min at the station is the safe figure.

Arrive Furongzhen.basis: Chinese guides call Furongzhen one of China's closest HSR stations to its scenic area (~5 km, 7-10 min by car, taxi under ¥20, shuttle minibuses waiting at the exit), so only deboarding and finding transport happens here.

Check in at Waterfall Bay.basis: Small family-run 民宿 inside the scenic area; check-in plus buying the ~¥108 multi-day ticket that guides quote is a 20-30 min errand.

Liu Xiaoqing rice tofu.basis: Ctrip/Mafengwo reviews: ¥5 a bowl at No. 113 by the archway, shop is tiny and packed so people eat under the outdoor awning or walk with it — a snack stop, not a sit-down lunch.

Wuli Stone Street.basis: The 5-li (2.5 km) street is the town's spine, but guides say the whole core loop is walkable in about an hour brisk / two hours relaxed, so an unhurried first pass with shops and photos is about 60 min.

Tuwang Palace.basis: Blogs treat 土司/土王行宫 as a compact clifftop wooden complex and 'another great photo spot' over the waterfall (part of it now a guesthouse) rather than a museum you work through.

Xizhou Bronze Pillar.basis: It is a single 5-tonne column displayed in the small 铜柱园 / folk-customs hall on the standard walking loop; photo-spot listings give it one line, so 15-25 min covers the pillar and its panels.

Furong waterfall.basis: Guides advise 20-30 min to walk the full waterfall walkways before shooting seriously, and the loop here also takes in the viewing platform, water-curtain cave behind the 60 m falls and the covered bridge below.

Youshui River cruise.basis: Trip reports describe the Youshui boat as 'a very short ferry' (bundled at ¥68 with the shuttle, running ~09:00-18:00); no source gives a duration, so 30 min covers boarding, wait and the run past the falls.

Far-bank platform.basis: Photo-spot roundups list the opposite-bank/观景台 as a single fixed vantage where visitors gather for sunset and the illuminated falls; it is a stand-and-shoot stop, not a walk.

Shenpu Camp Square.basis: Could not verify this square by name in any Chinese or English source; treated as one more open viewpoint on the night circuit, and squares here read as short stand-and-look stops.

Baishetang Square.basis: Scheduled free performances at 摆手堂 run at 10:30, 16:30 and 19:30 (plus a 20:30 theatre show, moved indoors if raining); a square set of Tujia songs, 摆手舞 and 茅古斯 runs roughly half an hour.

Dawn photo session.basis: Guides name 07:00-09:00 as one of the two good photography windows; walking out to a viewpoint, waiting for the mist to lift and shooting the empty flagstones is a 45 min outing.

Old-town mop-up.basis: Flex block; guides put the full sight-by-sight loop at 4-6 h versus 3-4 h for a selective visit, leaving about an hour of genuine second-pass material (behind-the-falls walkway, Tuwang Palace).

Check in at RongShi.basis: China hotel check-in requires passport scan and police registration; trip reports consistently put this at 15-30 min for a small downtown hotel.

Reed Flute Cave.basis: Guides and visitor reports agree the one-way U-shaped route (240 m of cave) runs 40-60 min in a guided batch, with 1-1.5 hr total from ticket gate to exit.

Elephant Trunk Hill.basis: Viewing the hill free from the promenade/Love Island viewpoint is a photo stop of 30-45 min; only entering the paid park pushes it to the 1-2 hr range quoted for the full grounds.

Two Rivers & Four Lakes.basis: Operators and review sites put the full Two Rivers & Four Lakes night cruise at 80-90 min over ~7 km (the shorter Four Lakes-only loop is ~60 min).

Land at LJG.basis: LJG is a small single-terminal domestic airport; deplane to curbside with checked bags runs 30-45 min including bus-to-terminal on remote stands.

Check in at Anyin.basis: Guesthouse check-in is 15-20 min, but Lijiang sits at 2,400 m and altitude guidance (and the plan's own note) is to rest an hour before walking.

Dayan Old Town.basis: Guides give the old town half a day to a full day overall; 90 min covers a focused wander of the quieter northern canal lanes as one of several old-town stops.

Sifang Square.basis: Reviews treat Sifangjie as a short stop - the liveliest spot for people-watching, but it is one plaza with four streets radiating off it.

Mu Mansion.basis: Guides recommend 1-2 h for the full interior (CNY 40, 08:30-17:30), but the plan admires it from outside - facade, gate and forecourt is 30-45 min; add 60-90 if you go in.

Depart for the gorge.basis: Chinese long-distance bus stations require ID check plus bag security and advise arriving ~30 min before departure; a private driver would cut this to ~10 min.

Qiaotou gateway.basis: Qiaotou (Hutiaoxia town) is where the gorge entrance fee is paid and onward vans are arranged; trip reports describe 20-40 min of formalities and waiting.

Tiger Leaping Gorge.basis: China Highlights and other guides put the Upper Gorge scenic spot at 1-2 hours on the paved plank path down to the tiger statue and back up the stairs.

Middle Gorge descent.basis: Trip reports consistently give 2-3 h for the descent from Tina's to the river and the steep climb back via Teacher Zhang's trail or the 168-step Sky Ladder.

Glacier Park cable car.basis: Chinese guides report 1-2 h queuing at the Ganhaizi transfer station and big-cableway boarding area as normal in July-August (20,000+ visitors/day), plus the ~20 min ride; English sources warn of up to 3 h in peak summer - an early timed slot is essential.

Jade Dragon summit.basis: From the 4,506 m terminal the plank boardwalk climbs to 4,680 m; guides describe roughly a 1.5 h leisurely walk, and at this altitude everyone moves slowly and stops often - includes starting the descent queue.

Impression Lijiang.basis: The show itself is exactly 60 min, but standard tickets are unreserved first-come seating and operators advise arriving up to an hour early; 30-35 min pre-show plus exiting the amphitheatre is realistic.

Blue Moon Valley.basis: The boardwalk from Upper Lake to Lower Lake is about 3 km; guides say 1-1.5 h is enough for both walking and photography if you skip the shuttle.

Old Town massage.basis: Old Town parlours sell 60- and 90-min sessions; a 60-min treatment plus changing, tea and paying lands at about 75 min.

Baisha Village.basis: Guides give Baisha 2-3 h in total; with the murals and embroidery institute counted separately, 75 min covers the main street, farm lanes and mountain views.

Baisha Murals.basis: The 55 surviving Ming-Qing panels sit in a handful of small halls (CNY 30); TripAdvisor reviewers describe a compact 30-45 min visit, longer only with a guide.

Baisha embroidery.basis: TripAdvisor reviewers call it worth 10-20 min to see the pieces and artists at work; listings quote up to an hour, so 30 min covers a genuine look plus a browse.

Shuhe Old Town.basis: Guides recommend 3-4 h for a full Shuhe visit, but for travellers who have already walked Dayan, 2 h covers the core lanes, canals and Qinglong Bridge; museum and lunch are separate stops.

Tea Horse Road Museum.basis: Listings give a recommended 0.5-1 h; reviewers note it is small with mostly Chinese-only captions, so 40 min covers the halls and the Ming murals at Dajue Palace.

Lashi Lake wetland.basis: Standard packages are ~1 h on horseback along the Tea Horse Road plus a ~45 min boat trip; with saddling up, changing boats and payment, on-site time is about 2.5 h.

Black Dragon Pool.basis: Guides and visitors put the park at 1-2 h to circle the water, cross the marble bridge and shoot the Jade Dragon reflection; some reviewers say 2 h still felt short.

Lion Hill sunset.basis: The climb from the old town is 15-20 min of steps, Wangu Tower is CNY 35 with five floors, and photographers advise arriving an hour before sunset for the golden light on the roofs.

Last Dayan loop.basis: Reviewers note Sifangjie is empty around 07:30 and you can wander freely for about 45 min before tour groups arrive at 10:00; an hour covers a relaxed farewell loop.

Fly from LJG.basis: Chinese domestic guidance is to arrive 2 h before departure; LJG counters close 45-60 min out, matching the plan's own 16:20 arrival for an 18:20 flight.

Land at PVG.basis: PVG guides put full international arrival at ~60min; a domestic arrival (HO1148 from Guilin, T2) skips immigration, leaving deplane, long terminal walk and belt wait at ~35-45min.

Shanghai Maglev.basis: Operator and airport guides: 8-minute run PVG-Longyang Road with departures every 15-20min, so ticket, platform wait, ride and exit total roughly 25min.

Check in at Marriott.basis: Standard city-hotel check-in plus bag drop and a quick freshen-up; no evidence of unusual delays at this property.

Nanjing Road East.basis: Guides say the full pedestrian street takes about two hours and 2-3h combined with the Bund; a one-way walk toward the river with browsing stops is about an hour.

The Bund.basis: GPSmyCity self-guided Bund route is 1.1km / about 1 hour, matching blog reports of 45-90min strolling the promenade.

Recovery massage / spa.basis: Shanghai spa listings (Time Out, SmartShanghai, Culture Trip) show 60-80min foot/body packages as the standard tourist option; add foot bath, changing and tea for ~90min door to door.

Jing’an Temple.basis: Multiple guides recommend about 1 hour for the compact walled complex (90min quoted as a generous middle ground); 45min is tight once you include ticketing and the Mahavira Hall.

Zhangyuan.basis: Reviews describe a restored shikumen retail precinct 'similar to Xintiandi but much quieter'; an unhurried wander of the lanes with a pop-up or two runs about an hour.

Nanjing Road West.basis: Shopping guides: most visitors spend 1-2h on West Nanjing Road, 2-3h if working through Plaza 66 / HKRI Taikoo Hui; 75min covers the strip plus one mall.

Dinner alt · Donghu Rd.basis: Same standard as a proper Shanghai sit-down dinner; Concession restaurant strips are relaxed rather than quick-turnover.

Wukang Building.basis: Walking guides treat Wukang Mansion as a photo landmark on the corner (best 16:00-17:30); it is exterior-only, so 15-25min including crowd jostling.

Wukang Road.basis: Guides quote 2-3h for Wukang Road with photos and coffee, but that bundles Ferguson Lane and cafes which are separate stops here; the 1.17km street alone walks in about an hour.

Ferguson Lane.basis: Ferguson Lane (376 Wukang Rd) is described as a small tucked-away courtyard of galleries and bistros — 15min to look, 45min if you actually sit for the coffee it exists for.

Anfu Road.basis: Wukang+Anfu combined walking routes are quoted at 3-4h over 2.5km; Anfu Road's own share, browsing a couple of shops, is roughly 45min.

Wulumuqi Road.basis: Guides frame Wulumuqi Middle Road as a short local-life detour (markets, Art Deco corner at Fuxing West Rd) rather than a destination; ~30min walk-through.

Sinan Mansions.basis: Travel guides advise 1-2h to walk the estate, admire the facades and browse boutiques/side galleries; 60min is the lower, unhurried-but-not-lingering end.

Fuxing Park.basis: Guides say Fuxing Park is 'worth a 30-60 minute walk'; 45min lets you watch the dancing and chess without circling twice.

Old Jazz Bar.basis: The Fairmont Peace Hotel Old Jazz Band plays a long nightly run (from ~18:30, sets through 23:30); reviewers describe staying for a couple of sets over drinks, roughly 90min.

Dinner alt · Fumin Rd.basis: Same standard as a proper Shanghai sit-down dinner; alternative Concession strip with comparable relaxed pace.

Yu Garden.basis: TripAdvisor/guide consensus is ~2h for a complete visit and 45-60min for a fast loop; at opening with fewer crowds, a highlights-plus circuit of the rockeries and pavilions is ~90min.

Yuyuan Bazaar.basis: Guides say you can 'easily spend an hour or two' in the bazaar alone (4h if you do garden, bazaar and dumpling houses together); 60min covers snacks and a souvenir sweep.

Mid-Lake Teahouse.basis: TripAdvisor reviewers report lingering 'an hour or two' over tea and the complimentary quail-egg/sweet snacks while watching the pond; 45min feels rushed for a set tea service.

City God Temple.basis: Guides quote 1-2h but that usually bundles the surrounding market; the walled temple itself (CNY10, 09:00-17:00) is compact and reads in ~45min.

People’s Square.basis: TripAdvisor reviews split between '10 minutes is plenty' for the plaza and 2-4h if you linger in People's Park; 45min suits its role here as a stroll-and-rest buffer.

M50 Creative Park.basis: Travel guides budget 2-4h (about 3h recommended) for 140+ studios and galleries plus the graffiti wall; 2h is a highlights-plus pass through the better galleries.

Huangpu night cruise.basis: Operators list the standard Shiliupu night cruise at 45-50min afloat; ticket redemption, security and boarding queues at the wharf add ~25min.

West Bund riverside.basis: No dedicated dwell figure found; the Xuhui riverside corridor linking the museums is a 10-15min walk each way, so ~45min allows an unhurried stroll with stops between venues.

West Bund Museum.basis: Museum lists 11:00-18:00 with last entry 17:00 across a modest number of galleries; guides recommend several hours only for major shows, so a highlights-plus visit is ~90min.

Long Museum West Bund.basis: TripAdvisor reviewers say 'about an hour to see it', some 'squeeze in two hours', and guides suggest 3-4h only for a blockbuster temporary show; 90min is the unhurried middle.

TANK Shanghai.basis: Some visitors suggest half a day, but TripAdvisor reviews repeatedly call the exhibits limited for the ticket price; the tanks plus the wrapping park read in about 75min.

Check in — J Hotel (Tower).basis: J Hotel's reception is on floor 101 of Shanghai Tower (check-in 15:00), so lift-lobby routing, the shuttle-lift ride and a luxury check-in run longer than a street-level desk.

Shanghai Tower base.basis: No published dwell time; the ground plaza and Exit 9A photo spot are the documented ground-level draws, and a walk around the base with photos is ~30min.

Jin Mao Tower.basis: Treated per the note as an exterior stop; going up would be different — the 88F deck is quoted at 2-3h and the Skywalk session alone is 45min plus 30min security check-in.

World Financial Center.basis: Exterior stop per the note; the 94/97/100F observatory would instead need 1-2h (30min on 94F, 20min on 97F, 1-1.5h on 100F) plus ticket and lift queues.

Shanghai Museum East.basis: Guides advise at least 2-3h and recommend 3-4h (3-5h thorough) for 20 halls; 3 focused hours covers the headline galleries plus one temporary show.

Pudong promenade.basis: Binjiang Avenue full route logs are 7.7km/2h, but the Lujiazui section fronting the towers is a fraction of that; TripAdvisor describes it as a short skyline stroll of ~45min.

Oriental Pearl Tower.basis: Exterior-only per the note, so a photo stop at the base; ascending instead runs 1-2h on the decks and 2-3h with the museum, plus 15-60min ticket and 10-60min lift queues.

Fly from PVG.basis: PVG guidance is to arrive 3h before an international departure (check-in closes 60min out), with Aug listed among the airport's busiest months; matches the note's 23:10 for a 02:10 flight.

Zhujiang Wharf transfer.basis: Li River operators require arrival 30-45 min before sailing: passport checked twice (ticket machine, then boarding hall), with boarding opening 30 min pre-departure.

Li River cruise.basis: 4-star boats from Zhujiang Pier to Yangshuo Longtoushan Pier sail 4-4.5 hrs over 83 km (faster only when water is unusually high); 09:20 departure lands ~13:30.

Fengqi Homestay.basis: China guesthouse check-in needs passport scan and police registration; small homestays typically take 15-30 min including bag drop.

West Street.basis: TripAdvisor and guides describe West Street as an evening hangout where a wander plus riverfront takes 1-1.5 hr before it becomes bar-hopping rather than sightseeing.

Impression Liu Sanjie.basis: Show runs ~70 min (operators quote 60-70); the venue advises arriving well before curtain and the 2,000+ seat amphitheatre empties slowly, so allow ~20 min of seating and exit.

Xianggong sunrise.basis: About 400 steps, 15-30 min up, then reviewers wait and shoot at the top through sunrise before descending; sunrise trip reports put on-hill time at 1-1.5 hr.

Yulong bamboo rafting.basis: Route tables for Yulong rafting list Jinlong Bridge to Jiuxian as 6 km / 90 min, the longest and most popular section with its nine small weirs.

Yulong valley cycling.basis: The West Street round-trip loop through the Shili Gallery / Jiuxian-Chaoyang Weir section is 19 km and quoted at 2-3 hrs by cycling guides, including photo and drink stops.

Moon Hill.basis: 800+ stone steps; guides quote ~30-40 min to the arch (China Highlights says ~1 hr to the top), plus time at the arch and the descent, and August heat slows everyone down.

Li River night walk.basis: Optional after-dinner stroll on the Yangshuo riverfront promenade; no fixed route, and 30-45 min covers the illuminated stretch near West Street.

Sunrise balloon flight.basis: Operators quote ~45-60 min airborne inside a 4-5 hr door-to-door experience; on-field time with inflation, briefing, landing and packing runs about 2 hrs.

Xingping Ancient Town.basis: Guides call the old town compact enough to walk in 10-15 min of pure walking, but visitors report 30-60 min with the old street, ferry pier and riverside stops.

20-RMB viewpoint.basis: Once on site it is a photo stop; reviewers spend 20-30 min queuing for the exact banknote angle and shooting, with the ~15-20 min riverside walk counted as travel.

Fly from KWL.basis: Guilin Liangjiang guidance is to arrive 2 hrs before a domestic departure (counters close 40-60 min prior), matching the itinerary's 08:20 arrival for a 10:20 flight.

Arrive Zhangjiajie West.basis: Guides: Tourist Distributing Center is ~1 min from the station exit and Wulingyuan buses leave every ~10 min, so deboarding, ticketing and boarding runs ~30 min.

Check in at Yuji Hotel.basis: Standard Chinese hotel check-in plus the mandatory foreign-passport police registration typically runs 20-30 min even at a small Wulingyuan hotel.

Wulingyuan East Gate.basis: Park uses real-name face-recognition entry; one traveller reported standing 40 min at the East Gate with a passport, and guides tell foreigners to arrive 45 min early to clear security.

Golden Whip Stream.basis: Trail guides and trip reports put the full 7.5 km flat walk at 2.5-3 h at a relaxed pace with photo stops (some quote 3-4 h).

Bailong Elevator.basis: Ride is only 92 seconds but peak-season (May-Oct) queues run 1-2 h and worse on summer mornings; arriving at the 07:00 opening is the one way to hold it near 30-45 min.

Yuanjiajie (Avatar).basis: Guides put Yuanjiajie at 2-3 h (photographers 3-4 h); the loop trail is 1-2 h walking but viewing platforms are shoulder-to-shoulder after 09:00 and inter-stop shuttles queue 20 min+.

Tianzi Mountain.basis: He Long Park alone is recommended at 1-1.5 h and the classic Tianzi route at 2-3 h; add free-shuttle waits of 20 min or more between Imperial Brush Peaks and Fairy Scattering Flowers.

Tianzi cableway down.basis: Ride is 6 min 26 s, but peak-summer queues at the Tianzi cableway reach 2 h and only drop under 15 min after 16:00 — an afternoon descent realistically costs about an hour.

Ten-Mile Gallery.basis: Official guidance is ~1 h for the 2 km gallery; tram is 10-15 min each way and the walk-out ~40 min, so tram queue plus walk lands near 1.5 h in August.

Yangjiajie cableway.basis: Ride is 5 min 12 s and Yangjiajie is the park's quietest developed area with only moderate queues, so ~30 min of waiting is realistic even in peak season.

Yangjiajie.basis: Most visitors do the northern highlights in 3-4 h; Natural Great Wall is ~20 min near the cable station and One Step to Heaven ~1 h from Wulong Village plus 15 min viewing, so 2.5 h covers the core without Tianbo Mansion.

Bus to Zhangjiajie city.basis: Wulingyuan bus station departures to the city run every ~20-30 min; ticketing, bag handling and boarding wait total about half an hour before the ~1 h ride.

Tianmen cableway.basis: Line C is a 20-min shuttle to the mountain gate then a 7-min express cableway to Tianmen Cave, with reported express-cableway queues of 30-45 min in peak season.

Tianmen Mountain.basis: Trip reports put a full Tianmen visit at 5-7 h including waits (Line C 4.5-5.5 h): summit 2-3 h, West Line cliff walkway ~2 h, 999 steps 20-30 min, each glass skywalk 5-10 min, plus escalator and descent-bus queues — with the cableway stop this is ~5.5 h, most of the day.
